test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following methods of depreciation is prescribed by the Income Tax Act, 1961?
solution:
The correct answer is** Written-down value method.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Written-down value method:**

 
 
• This method is prescribed by the Income Tax Act, 1961 for calculating depreciation for tax purposes.
 
• In the written-down value (WDV) method, depreciation is calculated on the book value of the asset, which reduces each year. This results in higher depreciation expenses in the initial years and lower expenses in the later years.
 
• This method aligns with the principle of matching expenses with revenues, as assets are typically more productive in their earlier years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sum-of-years-digits method:**

 
 
• This method accelerates depreciation, similar to the written-down value method, but is not prescribed by the Income Tax Act, 1961.
 
• Depreciation is calculated by multiplying the depreciable amount by a fraction, which decreases each year. This method is more complex and less commonly used for tax purposes.
 
 
 
• **Production hour method:**
 
 
• This method calculates depreciation based on the actual usage or production hours of the asset, making it suitable for machinery and equipment.
 
• However, it is not prescribed by the Income Tax Act, 1961 for calculating tax depreciation.
 
 
 
• **Double-declining balance method:**
 
 
• This is another accelerated depreciation method where depreciation is calculated at double the rate of the straight-line method.
 
• Although it provides higher depreciation expenses in the early years, it is not prescribed by the Income Tax Act, 1961 for tax purposes.
